entry.title: MLB: What to watch on September 26, 2026
entry.content:

Detail

Atlanta Braves @ Miami Marlins, 1:10p

Summary

This game is a mismatch of stakes wrapped in a Marlins tank-mode curiosity, but the Ralston debut and Suter's knuckleball-slow theatrics give it some juice. Atlanta has already clinched the NL East for the first time since 2023 and locked up a playoff spot, so the Braves are coasting into October while Miami plays out the string near .500. The Marlins, though, have quietly been the more watchable team by the numbers — Marlins hitters have an OBP of .332 against RHP this season, and a groundball batting average of .282 this season, both among the league's best — and their tNERD of 9.13 (youth, thrift, and a scrappy baserunning game) dwarfs Atlanta's more veteran, higher-priced 5.08. On the mound, 37-year-old Brent Suter, working as an emergency starter after mostly relieving, brings his molasses-paced delivery and grounder-heavy profile for a tidy 7.46 pNERD. Opposite him is Jack Ralston, making his first start of the season for Miami — total mystery box, hence the flat 0.00 pNERD. With a 13.34 gNERD, this sits comfortably above today's 10.31 average, worth a look if only to see how the rookie handles his moment.

Los Angeles Dodgers @ San Francisco Giants, 1:05p

Summary

A dominant Cy Young winner making a playoff-readiness tune-up start against a last-place club playing out the string — this one's mostly about watching Blake Snell, not the final score. The gNERD of 13.29 sits well above both the historic average (10.81) and today's slate average (10.31), driven almost entirely by the pitching mismatch. Snell, fresh off exiting his last start early with groin discomfort, returns with a 9.56 pNERD (near the top of today's range) fueled by elite strikeout stuff — his 4-1 record with a 1.86 ERA and 52 strikeouts in 38 2/3 innings and a filthy swinging-strike rate. He's looking to prove he's healthy and deserving of a spot in the postseason rotation rather than pile up innings, so don't expect a complete-game clinic. Across from him, rookie Matt Wilkinson has no pNERD data but has quietly been effective, having thrown five scoreless innings against this Dodgers lineup on 76 pitches six days ago. Team-wise, it's lopsided — LA's 8.93 tNERD dwarfs San Francisco's 3.09, and the Giants are 65-95, fourth in the division, and have lost 10 of its last 13. Watch for Snell's stuff, not the standings.

St. Louis Cardinals @ Milwaukee Brewers, 4:10p

Summary

Milwaukee's already popped the champagne on the division, but that doesn't mean this one's meaningless — it's the last look at Dustin May before October, and the underlying numbers say he's better than his line suggests. The Brewers, owners of the best team-NERD score of anyone playing today, have clinched their fourth straight NL Central title and a first-round bye, and it shows in the profile: a lineup with real pop, plus a bullpen and baserunning game that both grade out well above average. May, acquired from St. Louis at the deadline in a bit of irony given today's opponent, has had a rough September on the results side, but the recent line scores matter more than the strong overall numbers — his velocity is elite and his xFIP suggests he's due for better luck. Mathews, a rookie lefty, carries a 3.65 ERA over 44.1 innings and has been excellent lately, with three straight quality starts, though his NERD components (thin strike rate) are unspectacular. At 13.07, this game grades above today's 10.31 average and comfortably above the historical median, largely on the strength of Milwaukee's tNERD — one of the more well-rounded rosters on the schedule, even in a game that otherwise carries little playoff stakes.

Arizona Diamondbacks @ San Diego Padres, 5:40p

Summary

A win-or-else game with real playoff stakes, even if the pitching matchup is a bit of a mystery box. Arizona rolls into Petco riding a six-game winning streak and fighting for its postseason life, while San Diego is still trying to nail down the top NL Wild Card spot after dropping the series opener 11-4. Complicating things: Corbin Burnes just landed on the injured list, leaving the Diamondbacks without a starter and likely turning to a bullpen game — hence the TBD and its inevitable 0.00 pNERD. Walker Buehler takes the ball for the Padres instead, and while his strikeout stuff has faded (weak swinging-strike rate drags his component into negative territory), his xFIP- sits right at league average and his 4.56 pNERD gets a boost from some bad luck that could turn. San Diego's tNERD of 10.49 is well above the 95th percentile threshold, powered by an elite bullpen and one of the better broadcast booths in baseball. Add it up and the 12.96 gNERD clears today's average comfortably — a legitimately watchable game, mystery starter and all, especially with October implications on the line.

New York Mets @ Washington Nationals, 9:35a

Summary

Both the Mets and Nationals are playing out the string, but there's a genuinely fun subplot on the mound worth catching. Jonah Tong, still just 23 and finding his footing, has been inconsistent since his September call-up, with a 1-1 record and 4.60 ERA over his last four starts, though he's flashed real swing-and-miss stuff along the way. Across from him, Connelly Early makes his Nationals debut after not facing a major league hitter since June 30, dealing with elbow inflammation in July and a forearm setback in his recovery, a solid debut storyline for a team that paired one of the most potent offenses in the majors with one of the weakest rotations. Washington's tNERD (8.26) comfortably outpaces New York's (5.56), fueled by strong baserunning and a young, cheap roster, though a shaky bullpen drags it back down. Neither arm rates as a marquee pNERD performer, but both are young with age boosting their scores, and the strikeout/whiff data suggests occasional swing-and-miss appeal from Tong. With a gNERD of 11.66, this sits a bit above the historic median and roughly in line with today's slate average — not appointment viewing, but a decent watch for the two rookie-ish arms alone.

Tampa Bay Rays @ Philadelphia Phillies, 4:15p

Summary

The Rays have clinched everything, the Phillies are scrapping for a Wild Card, and this game is mostly a formality dressed up as playoff prep. Tampa Bay has already wrapped up the AL East and the AL's top seed, and their offense has been quiet lately, having "modest anyway" offense, scoring twice in Friday's game and going 6-4 over its previous 10. Philadelphia, meanwhile, is fighting for its playoff life, sitting in the final Wild Card spot and coming off a stretch where "the Phillies have scored only two runs during their current two-game losing streak"—not exactly a lineup peaking at the right time. The Phillies' starter is unannounced, which drags down the pitching side of this equation considerably. Griffin Jax is the reason to tune in early: he's coming off two straight scoreless outings since returning from the injured list, and his peripherals (strong strikeout rate, low xFIP-) back up the eye test. With a pNERD near 8—well above today's average of 4.98—Jax alone nudges this game above the pack. Overall gNERD of 10.89 sits just above the historical median, buoyed almost entirely by pitching intrigue rather than lineup firepower, given both teams' middling batting profiles this year.

Pittsburgh Pirates @ Detroit Tigers, 10:10a

Summary

Here's the story here, and it's got nothing to do with the numbers: this is Justin Verlander's final career start, and the Pirates counter with 39-year-old Kirby Yates making his first (and possibly only) start of the season—so buckle up for a farewell tour, not a pitching clinic. Verlander hasn't faced hitters in a game since June, his lone appearance this season lasted less than four innings, and his career line reads an unsightly 0-1 with an ERA north of 12—hardly the stuff of NERD legend, hence the pNERD goose-egg. Yates, working as bullpen-game opener for a so-so Pittsburgh relief corps, isn't walking in with much stuff-based hype either. Both pitcher scores land at zero simply because there's no real statistical projection for what amounts to ceremonial and improvised outings. The gNERD of 10.70 sits almost exactly at the historical median and slightly above today's average, propped up almost entirely by the Pirates' tNERD (7.53)—strong bullpen and baserunning numbers—against a middling Tigers squad (3.87) that's hot at the plate lately, ranking fourth in OPS this month. Watch this one for the sentimental send-off, not the stat line.

Cleveland Guardians @ Kansas City Royals, 4:10p

Summary

Cleveland's playing for a division title and a first-round bye, while Kansas City is mathematically eliminated and just trying not to embarrass itself in front of the home crowd — that stakes imbalance is the whole story here. This is the middle game of a three-game season-ending series, and Friday's opener was a wild one: Cleveland won the series opener 12-9, scoring five runs in the ninth inning aided by six walks from Kansas City relievers, while Royals catcher Carter Jensen homered twice and drove in a career-high five runs in the loss. That bullpen leakiness is a running theme — the Royals' pen grades out brutally in the underlying numbers, dragging Kansas City's tNERD down to 4.44, well below today's 5.33 average, even though Wacha has a 2.93 ERA at home this season, giving him the higher pNERD of the two starters at 4.22. Bibee, by contrast, is scuffling — that's actually a league-average pitcher at best, and it's trending in the wrong direction since the break, with Bibee's ERA sitting between a 4.02 and 4.79 estimator range — and his 2.68 pNERD reflects it. The 9.11 gNERD lands below the historic median, so this isn't essential viewing, but Cleveland's playoff stakes and a shaky Royals pen make a late blowup plausible.

Texas Rangers @ Minnesota Twins, 1:10p

Summary

Two teams playing out the string in a lost season find some juice from Nathan Eovaldi, who's quietly been the best thing going in this series. There's no pennant race drama here — the Rangers and Twins are both finishing well outside the postseason picture, so don't expect playoff intensity, just craftsmen doing craftsman things.

Eovaldi, at 36 and still humming it in around 94 mph, is the reason to tune in: his xFIP- of 85 and strong swinging-strike and strike-throwing rates push his pNERD to 7.76, comfortably above today's slate average, and his positive luck score suggests his solid results haven't even fully caught up to how well he's actually pitching. Bailey Ober, by contrast, brings a well-below-average fastball and an xFIP- north of 117, translating to a modest 2.21 pNERD — home half of a discount doubleheader. Team-wise, neither Rangers (4.86 tNERD) nor Twins (3.26) bring much thump; both are below-average on the basepaths and defensively shaky, with Minnesota's fielding runs a particular sore spot. The overall gNERD of 9.04 lands below both the historic and today's averages — watch for Eovaldi, not much else.

Summary

Colorado's a rebuilding disaster, Chicago's a team surging into the playoffs, and Jose Quintana's pNERD score suggests you'd get more entertainment value watching paint dry. This one's mostly about narrative gulf rather than baseball drama. The White Sox, locked into a playoff spot and looking to finish strong, have a spot in the American League playoffs assured but seeding still to be determined, and wins in five of the past six games entering Saturday show that Chicago is surging as the regular season concludes. Their tNERD of 8.58 is well above the historic 75th percentile, buoyed by a young, cheap roster that hits and fields better than average. Colorado, by contrast, sits at a miserable 1.71 tNERD, dragged down by poor batting, fielding, and barrel rates - fitting for a team already sitting at 57-102.

On the mound, Quintana is the story nobody wants to watch: at 37, he's made just 10 starts in his first season with Colorado amid injuries to his right hamstring and left elbow, and he's walking exactly 9% of batters faced for the second consecutive season while rocking a career-low 11.1 K%. His -2.48 pNERD is well below average. Davis Martin offers more hope, pitching effectively down the stretch with an 0.89 ERA in four September starts, though he's still hunting his first win since June. With a gNERD of 6.10, sitting below both the historic and today's averages, this is a game to skip unless you're already invested in a White Sox playoff run.

Cleveland Guardians @ Kansas City Royals, 4:40p

Summary

Cleveland's Gavin Williams is dealing his way through a division race, and this one carries real September stakes. The Guardians roll into Kauffman Stadium a game up in the AL Central with three to play, and Williams has been the reason why — over his last four starts he owns a 1.44 ERA over 25 innings with 40 strikeouts, and his last outing was seven scoreless against the Athletics. His pNERD of 12.85 backs that up, driven by elite whiff and strike rates plus mid-90s-and-up velocity, and it's one of the higher marks you'll see this year (today's pitcher scores top out at 12.85, so he's literally the best arm on the slate). Cameron is a serviceable lefty foil rather than a marquee name — solid in his own right at 9-8 with a 3.92 ERA and a 1.20 WHIP, with 155 strikeouts, 54 walks and 19 home runs allowed — but his 5.62 pNERD is merely average. Cleveland's bullpen (a real strength) and youth push their tNERD well above Kansas City's, whose bullpen has been a genuine liability. The Royals are playing out the string, but with a division on the line for Cleveland and a true frontline starter on the bump, this one's worth tuning in for.

Chicago Cubs @ Boston Red Sox, 2:35p

Summary

Both teams have already clinched playoff spots, so this is a doubleheader nightcap with meaningful baseball but low stakes for standings, and the pitching matchup is more interesting than the win-loss records suggest. David Peterson has quietly turned things around since being dealt to the Cubs, and since coming over to Chicago in June, he's notched a 3.94 ERA, 1.39 WHIP and 68 strikeouts over 75.1 innings across 14 starts, backing up his above-average pNERD thanks largely to a favorable xFIP- and a career-best luck reading suggesting more good outings ahead. Bello has been even better lately: over his last 13 appearances he owns a 2.28 ERA and 1.01 WHIP, with his latest turn his best of the year — eight innings at Tampa Bay, one run, no walks, 11 strikeouts. On the offensive side, Chicago's tNERD is elite thanks to strong batting and fielding runs, while Boston's bullpen has quietly been excellent, though Willson Contreras is sidelined and the Red Sox have scored just 63 runs since September 1st, the lowest mark in MLB. With a gNERD of 14.58 — well above the day's 11.55 average and near the top of the historical range — this is one of today's better watches, even if the standings drama is gone.

Detail

San Diego Padres @ Los Angeles Dodgers, 7:10p

Summary

This one's near the top of the pile for watchability, pairing a playoff-race gut-punch with the two best arms either roster can offer. The Padres just took sole possession of the NL wild-card lead by beating the Dodgers 5-1 behind a Manny Machado three-RBI game, snapping LA's 11-game home winning streak, so there's real juice left even with the Dodgers' division title already banked. Glasnow is the headline arm here, sitting at a 9.19 pNERD (well above today's 5.96 average) thanks to elite strikeout stuff and a barely-there xFIP-, and he's doing it in just his 13th start of the season after battling injuries — durability, not dominance, has been the question mark. Pivetta, making only his eighth start for similar reasons, still brings a strong xFIP- of his own. Both bullpens grade out well statistically, and San Diego's pen has Mason Miller, who has 37 saves and a 1.19 ERA, lurking if it stays close. With a gNERD of 17.24 comfortably above both the historical and today's averages, this is one of the better watches on the board.

Tampa Bay Rays @ New York Yankees, 4:05p

Summary

A season-finale AL East tune-up that still has one genuinely great pitching performance to watch. Cam Schlittler has quietly authored an ace-caliber campaign for the Yankees, and both teams have already locked up their postseason fates, so this is more showcase than survival — but Schlittler's stuff makes it worth tuning in regardless.

Schlittler's pNERD of 10.82 sits well above today's field (average 5.96, ranking near the historical 95th percentile), and it's earned: his four-seam fastball sits at 98.0 mph with a .232 xwOBA against and 31.5% whiff rate, backed by a curveball that generates a 41.7% whiff rate. He's been the best pitcher in the American League by ERA this season, sitting at 1.94 with a 14-6 record — though he's reportedly lined up for Tuesday's wild-card game, so a short leash is possible. Seymour is no slouch either (pNERD 8.85), riding elite xFIP-, but he's an ERA over 5.00 across his past five appearances. The Yankees' offense (tNERD 7.38) brings serious thump, especially second in xwOBA and first in barrel rate against left-handed pitching. With a gNERD of 15.78, comfortably above the daily and historical averages, this one's worth your remote — just don't expect either bullpen to stick around long.

Andrew Painter, Philadelphia's prized 23-year-old, has scuffled to a 5.59 ERA this season, but his pNERD of 7.72 comes from real stuff underneath — mid-90s velocity, a young arm, and a hefty positive luck score suggesting his results should be better than they've looked. Chicago sits a game back of Cleveland for the AL Central crown, and after Tuesday's wild 14-11 White Sox win and a 22-1 blowout earlier this season, the over has cashed in eight of the last nine meetings between these two AL Central rivals. David Sandlin brings real swing-and-miss stuff (his pNERD of 7.72 is well above average) but his results have been erratic — he allowed 14 runs across his last three starts, spanning just 15 innings, including five earned runs on seven hits in only four innings. Randy Dobnak, by contrast, is more finesse than power, with a modest 3.59 pNERD built mostly on a quick pace rather than stuff, and he was tattooed by the Pittsburgh Pirates last time out, allowing four runs, seven hits and two walks in just 3 2/3 IP. Chicago's tNERD of 8.60 stands out (youth, payroll efficiency, solid bullpen) against Kansas City's middling 4.43, dragged down by a rough bullpen but boosted by some positive regression luck. At 12.18 gNERD, this sits above the historical median and right around today's average — not a marquee game, but the stakes and scoring trends make it worth a glance.

Boston's own tNERD gets a boost from a hefty positive luck score, suggesting this offense has actually underperformed its true talent — a little scary for Cleveland given they're clinging to a rubber match in a tightening race. Both tNERD marks sit almost exactly at league average, with the Rangers' offense buoyed by a hefty positive luck score suggesting some overperformance that could cool off, while the Mets counter with a solid bullpen and one of the better broadcast booths in the sport. Net result: a modestly above-average 9.79 gNERD, worth tuning in largely to watch McLean work.

  • Pitcher 'no data': Pitchers only have a pNERD score once they've started at least one game and have at least 20 innings pitched. I also show 'no data' when I can't correctly link a starting pitcher with their stats.
  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Cleveland Guardians @ Boston Red Sox, 3:45p

Summary

This one's worth clearing your schedule for: a division-race pitching duel between two nasty lefties, with Cleveland trying to hold onto first place in the AL Central over its final six games. At 16.16, the gNERD score sits near the top of today's slate and well above the historic average, and it's easy to see why. Payton Tolle, Boston's 23-year-old rookie, brings a 10.48 pNERD — his fastball is up near 96 mph, his strikeout stuff is real, and he's fresh off the first immaculate inning by a Red Sox pitcher since Chris Sale's third career immaculate inning in 2021, plus a 14-strikeout gem against Oakland last month. Parker Messick isn't far behind at 8.38, an All-Star this year who allowed three runs over six innings with eight strikeouts in his last outing to push Cleveland into first. That context punches above what the raw 9.64 gNERD suggests — it lands right around league average, just below the historical midpoint of 10.8. Rodón's pNERD of 3.74 reflects a solid but unspectacular xFIP- of 101, boosted by a healthy swinging-strike rate but dinged by shaky strike-throwing; Martinez's 3.36 pNERD tells a similar story, elevated only by excellent command of the zone. Neither pitcher profiles as a must-watch arm on stuff alone. The Yankees' tNERD (7.35) outpaces Tampa's (4.83), largely thanks to New York's power-hitting barrel rate, while the Rays get docked hard for weak contact quality despite solid baserunning. Tampa Bay has produced just a 91 wRC+ against left-handed pitching, ranking 22nd in MLB, and now draws a southpaw whose strength attacks that weakness. Watch for playoff-race tension more than pitching artistry.

entry.title: MLB: What to watch on September 21, 2026
entry.content:
Here are today's MLB games, ordered by watchability, based on how interesting the teams and starting pitchers look. Higher is better. For more information, read this post.

Notes:

  • Pitcher 'no data': Pitchers only have a pNERD score once they've started at least one game and have at least 20 innings pitched. I also show 'no data' when I can't correctly link a starting pitcher with their stats.
  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Washington Nationals @ Detroit Tigers, 3:40p

Summary

Two pitchers, two Tommy John surgeries, two comeback stories — this game is basically a science experiment in rust, and that's exactly why it's worth a look. DJ Herz makes his first big-league start since September 2024, having missed two years recovering from Tommy John surgery, with a June setback further slowing things down. Opposite him, River Ryan makes his Detroit debut after being traded from the Dodgers to the Tigers, along with two other players, in exchange for Tarik Skubal, and hasn't pitched in the majors since 2024 himself. Neither arm has meaningful workload data this year — Herz reached only 65 pitches in his last Triple-A outing, putting roughly four innings as a realistic ceiling — so both pNERD scores sit at zero simply because there's nothing to measure yet, not because they're bad. The real juice here is on the offensive side: Washington's tNERD of 8.37 is buoyed by strong baserunning and barrel rates, though a shaky bullpen drags it back down. Detroit's tNERD is more middling. With two teams that have already checked out of the playoff race, today's 10.91 gNERD ranks solidly above the day's 9.18 average — worth watching mostly for the novelty, not the stakes.

Both these clubs are playing out the string, but there's a genuine reason to tune in: Trey Yesavage is back. Yesavage starts for Toronto in his first outing since left knee surgery, and is expected to throw about three innings before handing off to the bullpen, so the real drama may be whether Toronto's bullpen can protect a shaky first act. When healthy, Yesavage has been legitimately electric — he's quietly turned into one of the more intriguing arms in Toronto's rotation, sitting 5-5 with a 3.65 ERA and 91 strikeouts across 93.2 innings — and his youth (22) and strikeout stuff drive a solid 4.90 pNERD. Across the mound, Shane Baz has had a rough go: a 6-15 record, a 4.11 ERA, and a 1.35 WHIP — numbers that explain why Baltimore has had trouble stringing together quality starts all September. Toronto's offense is oddly punchless (bottom-of-the-barrel barrel rate drags their tNERD to 3.53) while Baltimore's 5.54 tNERD gets a boost from thump and bullpen work. Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ Baltimore Orioles, 4:20p

Summary

Here's the summary:

This one's near the top of the day's slate for a reason: Jacob Misiorowski is must-watch theater, and Baltimore's depleted lineup gives him plenty of room to work. Misiorowski, this year's presumptive NL Cy Young frontrunner, has a 1.89 ERA with a 2.08 xERA and a 2.19 FIP over 166.1 innings, averaging 100.5 mph with his fastball and striking out 243 batters. What makes the 24-year-old's season remarkable isn't just velocity — he's issued just 42 walks for a 6.6% BB%, a stunning turnaround for a guy who once walked hitters at a double-digit clip in the minors. His 15.00 pNERD is essentially max-scale, built on elite strikeout stuff, a hellacious xFIP-, and youth. Brandon Young, by contrast, offers a modest 3.40 pNERD and a fringe-average four-seamer. The Orioles are limping toward the finish line — fighting for playoff survival at 75-80 with a -28 run differential, without Jackson Holliday, Luis Robert Jr., Tyler O'Neill, and Ryan Mountcastle all injured simultaneously. Milwaukee's tNERD (9.85) reflects a genuinely fun, young, athletic roster with plus baserunning and bullpen depth. This gNERD of 16.96 sits well above today's average and near the top of the historical distribution — tune in for the Miz, stay for the mismatch.

Miami Marlins @ San Diego Padres, 1:10p

Summary

Playoff-race backdrop meets a season-finale-ish rubber match that's got more juice than the standings might suggest. The Padres (85-69) are locked in behind a deep, well-drummed bullpen and a fielding unit that's quietly been excellent, while the Marlins, playing out the string at 76-78, still bring real teeth against right-handed pitching this month. The Marlins quietly slot inside the Top-10 in average, wOBA, and SLG against righties this month, which matters because Fernando Tatis Jr. is crushing Alcantara's pitch mix, managing an impressive .333 ISO with a 20.7% barrel rate in their recent history — a genuine swing-through storyline worth tracking. Alcantara still pumps mid-to-upper-90s heat and posts the better pNERD of the two arms, though Buehler owns a middling 4.16 xFIP over the past 30 days, so neither is exactly locked in. San Diego's tNERD (10.93) ranks near the top of today's slate, boosted by a strong bullpen and top-tier broadcast crew, and the Padres bring real quality to Petco. The overall gNERD of 14.91 sits comfortably above both the historical and today's averages — a solidly watchable one, buoyed more by team quality and a live individual matchup than by big pitching numbers.

Summary

A near-desperate playoff push meets a 38-year-old ace looking every bit his Cy Young self — this one's got juice. Texas clings to a one-game lead over Houston in the AL West with a week left, and manager Skip Schumaker is leaning on deGrom to eat innings after the Rangers had to turn to their bullpen more often than they'd like in the first two games of the series, with Cal Quantrill exiting Saturday's game with lat tightness. DeGrom himself is a story worth watching regardless of stakes — he signed with Texas in 2023 and was named an All-Star again in 2025, and his pNERD of 11.40 (fueled by a filthy xFIP- of 72 and elite swinging-strike rate) ranks well above today's 5.89 average. Toronto's Spencer Miles, just 25, is quietly excellent too, posting a strong 8.52 pNERD off a stingy xFIP-. The Blue Jays are essentially playing out the string, three games out of the wild card, and their offense reflects it — bottom-of-the-barrel exit velocity drags their tNERD down to 3.53. Still, with a 14.50 gNERD comfortably above the 10.81 historical average, this is a legitimately watchable pitching matchup wrapped around real standings drama.

A pennant-race game with a wildly lopsided pitching matchup, but the Diamondbacks' desperation makes it watchable anyway. Arizona is in must-win territory, badly needing a win to keep its postseason hopes alive, while the Yankees roll in comfortably positioned in the AL East. Both teams get a "positive luck" bump too, meaning each has actually underperformed its skill markers lately, so regression optimists can dream. With a gNERD of 6.66, well below the historic average of 10.81 and today's slate average of 11.43, this game leans toward background viewing — worth a glance for Anderson's development, skippable otherwise.

The Rays are on the verge of their first AL East title since 2021, riding a dominant 53-26 home record, while the Red Sox are scrapping for a wild card spot and have been red-hot since July. Bello brings a 5.31 pNERD built on a tidy 95-mph fastball and a deceptively deliberate pace, though his well-documented struggle with left-handed power (1.46 HR/9 to lefties versus 0.38 to righties) makes him a live-wire against Tampa's lineup. Peralta, meanwhile, has been quietly excellent since escaping a rough Mets stint, posting a 3.86 ERA with Tampa and an even sharper 0.78 ERA over his last four outings, including a five-inning hitless effort — though his 4.03 pNERD reflects so-so strikeout command underneath the shiny recent results. Boston's bullpen (one of the league's best by runs saved) and a Rays offense that gets on base without much thump (rock-bottom barrel rate) round out a game that lands almost exactly at today's average gNERD of 10.46 — competent, competitive, but not must-see.

This one's got real playoff stakes and one of the better pitching matchups on the board today, making it an easy pick for tonight's watchlist. San Diego enters with a real postseason push, and Manny Machado has 28 home runs and Fernando Tatis Jr. has 170 hits, 91 runs, and 35 stolen bases, with Petco Park a fortress at 46-29 at home. Miami isn't just playing out the string either — 18 of their final 23 games are against clubs ahead of them in the standings, so there's spoiler drama in play. The Padres' 10.67 tNERD (among the day's best) is built on a stacked bullpen and strong glovework, while Miami's 9.05 mark leans on speed and a young, cheap roster overperforming its Pythagorean expectations — that positive luck score hints they've actually been unlucky given their skill level. On the mound, Nick Pivetta's xFIP- of 79 is quietly excellent, buoying his 6.91 pNERD, while Tyler Phillips brings solid velocity (95.7 mph) but a more middling profile at 4.76. Combined gNERD of 15.70 sits near the top of today's slate and well above the historical average — worth your evening.

The Mets, despite a five-game losing streak, still get a mild tNERD edge (5.37 vs 4.72) thanks to better barrel rates and a notably strong broadcast crew rating on both TV and radio. Neither team's bats are impressing anyone — both Philly and New York post negative batting-runs marks — but both bullpens are quietly solid, which should keep things competitive into the late innings.

Pitching-wise, we're flying blind: Philadelphia's starter is still TBD, and Mets righty Zac Thornton has no NERD data on file, though he's carrying a 3.44 ERA into the start. With both pNERD scores sitting at zero, this game's 10.04 gNERD lands almost exactly at today's slate average of 11.60 — not a must-watch, but the standings drama and a five-game Mets skid give it a pulse. The Phillies lead the season series, having won five of the nine meetings between these clubs, so there's a little history for the taking.

Detail

Milwaukee Brewers @ Pittsburgh Pirates, 9:35a

Summary

A late-season laugher on paper, but the NERD math says pay attention anyway. Milwaukee's Brewers, fresh off clinching the NL Central at a franchise-record 36 games over .500, are chasing a sweep in Pittsburgh, while a Pirates team playing out the string has quietly set a single-season home run record. The 18.44 gNERD sits near the top of today's slate (7.94–18.44) and comfortably above the historic 95th percentile of 15.6, driven by two lively lineups—Milwaukee's power-and-speed combo (tNERD 9.93) and Pittsburgh's surprisingly frisky bats (tNERD 7.08) despite shaky fielding. Harrison has struggled lately, giving up 19 runs across his last three outings, but he's dominated Pittsburgh specifically, going 2-0 in three career starts without allowing a run in 17 innings. His pNERD (10.55) reflects real swing-and-miss stuff and a positive luck score suggesting better days ahead. Dotel, just 23 and making only his second career start, brings a 1.36 WHIP in a limited big-league sample but nasty velocity that props up his 9.34 pNERD—worth watching for the arm talent alone.

The Dodgers can clinch the NL West today, but the pitching matchup itself is more "watch for chaos" than "watch for craftsmanship."
